'''Vy Maria Dong''' (born 1976 in [[Big Spring, Texas|Big Spring]], [[Texas]]) is a Vietnamese-American Chancellor's Professor of Chemistry at the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI). Dong works on [[Enantioselective synthesis|enantioselective catalysis]] and [[natural product]] synthesis.<ref name=":0"/> She received the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s [[List of Royal Society of Chemistry medals and awards|Merck, Sharp & Dohme Award]] in 2020,<ref name=":8">{{Cite web|title=Professor Vy Dong {{!}} Merck, Sharp & Dohme Award winner 2020|url=https://www.rsc.org/awards-funding/awards/2020-winners/professor-vy-dong/|access-date=2021-06-09|website=Royal Society of Chemistry|date=2 April 2020 |language=en-GB}}</ref> the [[American Chemical Society]]'s [[Elias James Corey Award]] in 2019,<ref name=":6">{{Cite web|title=2019 National Award Recipients - American Chemical Society|url=https://www.acs.org/content/acs/en/funding-and-awards/awards/national/recipients/2019-national-award-recipients.html|access-date=2018-11-04|website=American Chemical Society|language=en}}</ref><ref name=":9">{{Cite web|title=Professor Vy Dong to receive the 2019 ACS E.J. Corey Award {{!}} UCI Department of Chemistry|url=https://www.chem.uci.edu/node/21576|access-date=2018-11-04|website=chem.uci.edu|language=en}}</ref> and the UCI's Distinguished Alumni Award in 2018.<ref name=":10">{{Cite web|date=April 17, 2018|title=Dong and Evans lauded {{!}} UCI Department of Chemistry|url=https://www.chem.uci.edu/node/20864|access-date=2021-06-09|website=www.chem.uci.edu}}</ref><ref name=":11">{{Cite web|title=UCI Lauds and Laurels Distinguished Alumni Award {{!}} UCI Department of Chemistry|url=https://www.chem.uci.edu/node/22107|access-date=2021-06-09|website=www.chem.uci.edu|archive-date=2021-06-09|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210609031120/https://www.chem.uci.edu/node/22107|url-status=dead}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Dong was born in [[Big Spring, Texas|Big Spring]], [[Texas]], in 1976, where she spent her early childhood, and moved with her family to [[Anaheim, California]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.chem.uci.edu/~dongv/about.html|title=The Dong Research Group - About Professor Vy M. Dong|last=Dong|first=Phi|website=chem.uci.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-11-04}}</ref><ref name=":3">{{Cite web|title=Vy M. Dong {{!}} ps.uci.edu|url=https://ps.uci.edu/node/46813|access-date=2018-11-04|website=ps.uci.edu|language=en|archive-date=2019-04-03|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190403014441/https://ps.uci.edu/node/46813|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref name=":7">{{Cite web|last=Taylor|first=Alexandra A.|date=April 30, 2019|title=Career Ladder: Vy Dong|url=https://cen.acs.org/people/profiles/Career-Ladder-Vy-Dong/97/i18|access-date=2021-05-14|website=cen.acs.org}}</ref> The first in her family to attend college, she studied chemistry at the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI) as a Regents' Scholar.<ref name=":7" /><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|title=UCI Magazine Fall 2018 -- The American Dream|language=en|work=Issuu|url=https://issuu.com/ucimagazine/docs/2018_fall_uci_magazine/36|access-date=2018-11-04|archive-date=2019-12-11|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20191211154219/https://issuu.com/ucimagazine/docs/2018_fall_uci_magazine/36|url-status=dead}}</ref> Dong decided to study chemistry during her sophomore year after taking a class with [[Larry E. Overman]], whom she later conducted undergraduate research with. She graduated ''[[magna cum laude]]'' in 1998 from UCI.

For her graduate studies, Dong attended the [[University of California, Berkeley]], joining [[David MacMillan]]'s lab as one of his first graduate students.<ref name=":4">{{Cite web|title=2016 Agnes Fay Morgan Research Award|url=http://www.iotasigmapi.info/awards/agnesfaymorgan/2016.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105061853/http://www.iotasigmapi.info/awards/agnesfaymorgan/2016.pdf|archive-date=2018-11-05|access-date=2018-11-04|website=IOTA Sigma Pi}}</ref> She moved with MacMillan to the [[California Institute of Technology]], earning her PhD there in 2004. Her thesis featured work on variants of a [[zwitterion]]ic-[[Claisen rearrangement]],<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Yoon|first1=Tehshik P.|last2=Dong|first2=Vy M.|last3=MacMillan|first3=David W. C.|date=1999-10-01|title=Development of a New Lewis Acid-Catalyzed Claisen Rearrangement|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja9919884|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=121|issue=41|pages=9726–9727|doi=10.1021/ja9919884|bibcode=1999JAChS.121.9726Y |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dong|first1=Vy M.|last2=MacMillan|first2=David W. C.|date=2001|title=Design of a New Cascade Reaction for the Construction of Complex Acyclic Architecture: The Tandem Acyl-Claisen Rearrangement|url=https://pubs.acs.org/doi/full/10.1021/ja005925t|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=123|issue=10|pages=2448–2449|doi=10.1021/ja005925t|pmid=11456904 |bibcode=2001JAChS.123.2448D |issn=0002-7863}}</ref> and their application towards a [[total synthesis]] of the [[natural product]] erythronolide B.<ref>{{Cite thesis|url=https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/754/|title=Novel Variants of the Zwitterionic Claisen Rearrangement and the Total Synthesis of Erythronolide B|last=Maria|first=Dong, Vy|date=2004|website=thesis.library.caltech.edu|doi=10.7907/AR3C-3566|access-date=2018-11-04|type=phd|archive-date=2018-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105012552/https://thesis.library.caltech.edu/754/|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Dong then moved back to UC Berkeley, working on supramolecular chemistry with [[Robert G. Bergman]] and [[Ken Raymond]] as a [[National Institutes of Health|NIH]] Postdoctoral Fellow.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://ucistories.lib.uci.edu/people/vy-dong|title=Vy Dong {{!}} UCI Stories|website=ucistories.lib.uci.edu|language=en|access-date=2018-11-04}}</ref> Her work with Bergman and Raymond focused on the development of a [[Supramolecular chemistry|supramolecular host molecule]] that can stabilize reactive [[Iminium|iminium ions]] in water.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Dong|first1=Vy M.|last2=Fiedler|first2=Dorothea|last3=Carl|first3=Barbara|last4=Bergman|first4=Robert G.|last5=Raymond|first5=Kenneth N.|date=2006-10-18|title=Molecular Recognition and Stabilization of Iminium Ions in Water|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=128|issue=45|pages=14464–14465|doi=10.1021/ja0657915|issn=0002-7863|pmc=2562236|pmid=17090022|bibcode=2006JAChS.12814464D }}</ref>

== Research and career ==
Dong began her independent career in 2006 at the [[University of Toronto]]. At Toronto, she worked on [[Heterocyclic compound|heterocycles]] for medicinal chemistry. She demonstrated how [[lactone]]s could be synthesized from [[Ketone|keto]]-[[aldehyde]]s using [[rhodium]] catalysts, achieving regio- and enantioselective lactones without any waste products.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Shen|first1=Zengming|last2=Khan|first2=Hasan A.|last3=Dong|first3=Vy M.|date=2008-03-01|title=Rh-Catalyzed Carbonyl Hydroacylation: An Enantioselective Approach to Lactones|url=https://doi.org/10.1021/ja7109025|journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society|volume=130|issue=10|pages=2916–2917|doi=10.1021/ja7109025|pmid=18278919 |bibcode=2008JAChS.130.2916S |issn=0002-7863|url-access=subscription}}</ref> Dong was appointed the Adrain Brook Distinguished Professor at the [[University of Toronto]] in 2011.<ref name="Awards & Distinctions">{{Cite web|title=Awards & Distinctions|url=http://www.chem.utoronto.ca/chemistry/news.php|access-date=2018-11-04|website=chem.utoronto.ca}}</ref>

In 2013, Dong moved her research group to the [[University of California, Irvine]] (UCI).<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://cn.chem-station.com/chemists/2015/06/vy-m-dong.html|title=Vy M. Dong|date=2015-06-02|work=化学空间 Chem-Station|access-date=2018-11-04|language=en-US}}</ref> Early highlights of research at UCI include catalytic [[hydroacylation]] and the activation of aldehyde C-H bonds.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/never-shut-down-another-persons-ideas-/6362.article|title=Never shut down another person's ideas|work=Chemistry World|access-date=2018-11-04|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Murphy|first1=Stephen K.|last2=Bruch|first2=Achim|last3=Dong|first3=Vy M.|date=2014|title=Substrate-Directed Hydroacylation: Rhodium-Catalyzed Coupling of Vinylphenols and Nonchelating Aldehydes|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|language=en|volume=53|issue=9|pages=2455–2459|doi=10.1002/anie.201309987|issn=1433-7851|pmc=4140243|pmid=24478146}}</ref>  Dong demonstrated that [[rhodium]] catalysis could be used to make cyclic peptides, using entirely achiral building blocks and hydrogenation catalysts.<ref name=":5">{{Cite news|title=Round-the-ring catalysis makes cyclic peptides chiral|language=en|work=Chemistry World|url=https://www.chemistryworld.com/news/round-the-ring-catalysis-makes-cyclic-peptides-chiral/3009348.article|access-date=2018-11-04}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Le|first1=Diane N.|last2=Hansen|first2=Eric|last3=Khan|first3=Hasan A.|last4=Kim|first4=Byoungmoo|last5=Wiest|first5=Olaf|last6=Dong|first6=Vy M.|date=2018|title=Hydrogenation catalyst generates cyclic peptide stereocentres in sequence|journal=[[Nature Chemistry]]|language=En|volume=10|issue=9|pages=968–973|bibcode=2018NatCh..10..968L|doi=10.1038/s41557-018-0089-5|issn=1755-4330|pmc=6824594|pmid=30061616}}</ref> Rh-hydride catalysis permits enantioselective reduction and allows access to motifs popular in medicinal chemistry.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Chen|first1=Zhiwei|last2=Dong|first2=Vy M.|date=2017|title=Enantioselective semireduction of allenes|journal=[[Nature Communications]]|language=En|volume=8|issue=1|pages=784|doi=10.1038/s41467-017-00793-0|doi-access=free|issn=2041-1723|pmid=28978908 |pmc=5627242 |bibcode=2017NatCo...8..784C}}</ref> Dong has also reported an aldehyde-alkyne coupling strategy using a dual rhodium catalyst and amine [[Organocatalysis|organocatalyst]] system.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Cruz|first1=Faben A.|last2=Dong|first2=Vy M.|date=2017|title=Stereodivergent Coupling of Aldehydes and Alkynes via Synergistic Catalysis Using Rh and Jacobsen's Amine|journal=[[Journal of the American Chemical Society]]|language=EN|volume=139|issue=3|pages=1029–1032|doi=10.1021/jacs.6b10680|issn=0002-7863|pmid= 28074655|pmc=9141309 |bibcode=2017JAChS.139.1029C }} {{closed access}}</ref> Dong continues to explore new reagents, catalysts and strategies for organic synthesis.<ref name=":3" />

==Awards and honors==
Dong is the recipient of numerous awards for her research in organic chemistry. She was awarded an Ontario Research Fund grant in 2008. Dong delivered the inaugural [[Eli Lilly and Company|Eli Lilly]] Young lecture at the [[University of Wisconsin–Madison]] in 2009, where she discussed the catalytic transformations of C-H bonds.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|title=Eli Lilly Young Investigator Lecture - Professor Vy Dong {{!}} UW-Madison Department of Chemistry|url=https://www.chem.wisc.edu/content/eli-lilly-young-investigator-lecture-professor-vy-dong|access-date=2018-11-04|website=chem.wisc.edu|language=en-us|archive-date=2018-11-05|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181105062018/https://www.chem.wisc.edu/content/eli-lilly-young-investigator-lecture-professor-vy-dong|url-status=dead}}</ref> She was awarded an [[Alfred P. Sloan Foundation]] Fellowship in 2009 and a named an [[Amgen]] Young Investigator in 2010. In 2010 she was awarded the [[AstraZeneca]] Award in Chemistry.<ref>{{Cite journal|author=Anon|date=2011|title=Franco-Spanish Prize: C. Nájera / ACS Pure Chemistry Award: M. S. Sanford / AstraZeneca Award in Chemistry: V. M. Dong|journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition|language=en|volume=50|issue=4|pages=801|doi=10.1002/anie.201006893|bibcode=2011ACIE...50..801. |issn=1433-7851}}</ref> She won an [[Arthur C. Cope Scholar Award]] of the [[American Chemical Society]] in 2010 for her contributions to organic chemistry.<ref name=":1" /> In 2011, Dong won the [[Hoffmann-La Roche|Roche]] Excellence in Chemistry award.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Roche|date=May 23, 2011|title=Roche Symposium Showcases Accomplishments of Next Generation of Chemists|url=https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/roche-symposium-showcases-accomplishments-of-next-generation-of-chemists-122439958.html|access-date=2018-11-04|website=prnewswire.com|language=en}}</ref> Dong won a [[Novartis]] Chemistry Lecturer in 2012. She was awarded a Society of Synthetic Organic Chemistry in Japan (SSOJC) Lectureship,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Faculty Awards {{!}} UCI Department of Chemistry|url=https://www.chem.uci.edu/talk-us/awards/faculty|access-date=2018-11-04|website=chem.uci.edu|language=en}}</ref> and a [[Japan Society for the Promotion of Science]] Fellowship in 2013.<ref name=":0" /> In 2016, Dong was awarded the [[Iota Sigma Pi]] [[Agnes Fay Morgan Research Award]] for her exceptional research on catalytic [[hydroacylation]].<ref name=":4" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Awards for Professionals|url=http://www.iotasigmapi.info/awards/professionalawards.html|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170822100414/http://www.iotasigmapi.info/awards/professionalawards.html|archive-date=2017-08-22|access-date=2018-11-04|website=iotasigmapi.info}}</ref> Dong received the UCI's Distinguished Alumni Award in 2018,<ref name=":10" /><ref name=":11" /> the [[American Chemical Society]]'s [[Elias James Corey Award]] in 2019,<ref name=":6" /><ref name=":9" /> and the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]]'s [[List of Royal Society of Chemistry medals and awards|Merck, Sharp & Dohme Award]] in 2020.<ref name=":8" />

Dong has served as an associate editor of the [[Royal Society of Chemistry]] journal [[Chemical Science (journal)|''Chemical Science'']] since 2015.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Chemical Science welcomes Vy Dong as Associate Editor – Chemical Science Blog|url=http://blogs.rsc.org/sc/2015/02/18/chemical-science-welcomes-vy-dong-as-associate-editor/|access-date=2018-11-04|website=blogs.rsc.org|language=en-US}}</ref>

== Personal life ==
Dong met her future husband, Wilmer Alkhas, at the [[University of California, Irvine]].<ref name=":2" /> They have a son, Liam.
